title: How to Check and Configure NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage for Your Platform | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's GPUDirect Storage team released gds-diag, an open-source Python CLI (plus an optional agent skill for coding assistants such as Claude and Codex) that audits, diagnoses and suggests fixes for GPUDirect Storage deployments. It is a practical tooling post that lowers the operational friction of GDS and shows NVIDIA shipping agent skills alongside its infrastructure software.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's GPUDirect Storage team released gds-diag, an open-source command-line utility that assesses GDS environments, identifies problems and suggests improvements.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is investing in reducing deployment friction for its GPU data-path stack, which supports adoption of GDS in AI clusters.
insights.locator: The gds-diag tool was developed by the GPUDirect Storage team

insights.claim: gds-diag runs on any Linux system with Python 3.8 or newer and is distributed through the NVIDIA Magnum IO GitHub repository with no other dependencies.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Minimal dependencies make it trivial to adopt on existing GPU storage nodes.

insights.claim: GPUDirect Storage itself requires an NVIDIA datacenter-class GPU and CUDA Toolkit 12.2 or newer, although these are not dependencies of gds-diag.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Defines the hardware and software floor for GDS and ties the feature to datacenter GPUs.

insights.claim: NVIDIA says GDS provides a data path between GPUs and storage that increases bandwidth, minimizes latency and reduces CPU and memory utilization across platforms and workloads.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Core value proposition of GDS for AI data pipelines; vendor claim without numbers in this post.

insights.claim: The source code is published under Apache 2.0 and the agent skill under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, and NVIDIA is soliciting community contributions of diagnostic checks and file system support.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Open licensing invites storage vendors to add support, widening the GDS ecosystem.

insights.claim: gds-diag groups its subcommands into end-to-end checks, pre-install checks, post-install validation and deep diagnostics for containers and specific mount points, and an 'all' command runs a full sequence on a given path across bare metal, VMs and containers.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Container support including Kubernetes and Enroot shows GDS is expected in orchestrated AI clusters.

insights.claim: Findings carry FAIL, WARN, INFO or PASS badges, each with an explanation and mitigation plan, and the tool never modifies the system on its own.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Read-only design lowers risk for production operators; remediation remains human or agent driven.
insights.quote: gds-diag will not implement the mitigation plan or otherwise modify the system on its own.
insights.locator: The anatomy of a gds-diag finding

insights.claim: gds-diag can emit all reports as structured JSON via --json, so findings can be ingested into other tools or archived.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Enables fleet-level automation and monitoring of GDS readiness.

insights.claim: The support-matrix subcommand shows which storage and platform combinations GDS supports, and most distributed storage vendors present their file systems as nfs or nfs4, so that row covers a broad range of products.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: GDS compatibility reaches many third-party storage vendors via NFS, a signal for storage ecosystem exposure.

insights.claim: The config-audit subcommand reviews static configuration files and environment variable modifiers, and in the demo caught a misspelled entry in a candidate configuration.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Shows the tool targets common misconfiguration as the main source of GDS deployment problems.

insights.claim: The optional agent skill adds a natural-language orchestration layer that routes to subcommands, interprets results and can propose or carry out remediation, while leaving deterministic checks to the underlying CLI.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Pattern of deterministic tool plus LLM routing layer is a template for AI-assisted infrastructure operations.

insights.claim: gds-diag is validated with both Claude and Codex coding assistants, and NVIDIA recommends the AI agent mode where available.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: A hardware vendor treating third-party coding agents as a first-class interface for its infrastructure software is evidence of agent tooling becoming a standard distribution channel.
insights.quote: gds-diag is validated with both Claude and Codex

insights.claim: NVIDIA calls agents a capability multiplier for gds-diag, and the demo used Anthropic Claude Code CLI to diagnose and fix a container startup problem by editing the launch script, honoring local confirmation policies.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Illustrates agents performing ops remediation under human-set permission policies.
insights.quote: Agents are a capability multiplier for gds-diag

insights.claim: NVIDIA says gds-diag's modular design is a foundation for future checks on network transports, object storage systems and application frameworks.
insights.speaker: Phil Carns
insights.so_what: Hints at the roadmap for GDS beyond local and file storage; watch for object storage support.
